_what: fusion's compliance-guard configuration for THIS project. The guard hooks read it from the project root, on every guarded tool call, and merge it over the plugin's own defaults. Keys the parser does not recognise are ignored, which is why these underscore-prefixed notes can live in the file itself.
_inherits: As seeded, this file declares nothing — and a file that declares nothing inherits everything. The effective protected-path list is the plugin's own hooks/config.json, and it is deliberately NOT restated here: a copy would go stale, and a stale copy of a security-relevant list is worse than a pointer to the live one. Read the plugin's hooks/config.json to see what is protected. A path added to that default later protects this project too, without this file being touched.
_override: To change something, add the top-level key you want to change, in the same shape the plugin's hooks/config.json uses for it. The merge is per top-level key: the object you write REPLACES the plugin's object of that name whole — it is not merged field by field — and any field you leave out of your object falls back to fusion's built-in default, not to the plugin's file. That is what makes NARROWING the protected list possible, which a field-by-field merge could never express. Top-level keys you do not write are inherited untouched. A file that exists but is not valid JSON is dropped and reported as a guard advisory, never ignored in silence.
_gitTracked: This file belongs in version control, and that is the point of it living at the project root. It decides what the guard protects, so every change to it has to appear in a diff and pass through the same review as the rest of the project.
_protectsItself: Once this file exists on disk the guard protects it, whatever this file itself says — an agent cannot unprotect the configuration that governs it. Editing, moving or deleting it through a guarded tool call is denied. Change it yourself, in your own editor or terminal, where the guard never looks.
_inFusionsOwnSourceTree: In the fusion plugin's own repository the protected-path half of this file has no effect, because the write guard stands down there so that fusion can be developed on itself. The escalation settings still apply, since the git branch-switch policy stays active even there.
